brief: Design an interface for "Temporal Texture Weaving" — a tool where users manipulate the perceived passage of time in their daily routine by literally weaving temporal threads on a loom-like interface,

dominant_strengths: Restrained earthy palette with one purple accent suggests a tactile, loom-like sensibility appropriate to weaving metaphor
Clean uppercase tracked labels and thin hour ticks create a calm, almost archival temporal grid
Category icons are clearly differentiated and readable at a glance, aiding quick orientation
dominant_weaknesses: The 'loom' is empty — no threads, no weave, no warp/weft visualization, so the central metaphor is invisible
Massive negative space below the timeline feels unfinished rather than meditative; no manipulation affordances shown
No indication of how time is 'stretched' or 'compressed' — the temporal manipulation premise is entirely absent
fix_priorities: Render actual woven threads across the 24-hour grid with variable thickness/tension showing perceived time
Add direct-manipulation handles for stretching, compressing, or interlacing threads between categories
Introduce a secondary panel showing reflective state: rhythm, density, or felt-time vs clock-time
Tighten vertical composition so the loom occupies the full canvas instead of floating in whitespace
rationale.norman_balance: Mildly visceral via palette and icons, but behavioral interaction is nearly absent and reflective payoff is unrealized.
rationale.intent_fit: Only the scaffolding of a loom exists — the weaving, temporal distortion, and texture metaphors central to the brief are not yet expressed.
